shots.text: Coca-Cola gave away millions of free drinks. On purpose.
In eighteen eighty-seven, Coke was a drink almost nobody had tried.
Its owner, Asa Candler, had a risky idea. Don't sell it. Give it away.
He handed out handwritten tickets, each good for one free glass.
Soon the tickets traveled further, through magazines and the mail.
Anyone could walk into a soda fountain with one, and drink Coke for free.
The bet was simple. One free taste, and some people would come back and pay.
Roughly eight and a half million free drinks were given away this way.
By eighteen ninety-five, Coke was being served in every state.
The free glass was never a gift. It was advertising you could taste.
And Coca-Cola is widely considered the first company to ever offer coupons.
The first coupon in history was a free Coke.
